title: Digital Marketing and Digital Banking
subtitle: Market bank products on Ethiopia's mobile-first channels and turn sign-ups into active digital customers
summary: Learn the digital funnel, Ethiopia's main channels, clear and compliant content in local languages, and how to drive real use of digital banking, ending with a campus content plan.
audience: Marketing, digital banking, product and branch staff of Ethiopian banks and microfinance institutions. No prerequisites.
objectives: Explain the digital marketing funnel and the main digital channels used in Ethiopia
Create compliant, clear digital content for bank products in Amharic, English and other local languages
Explain rates, fees and total costs honestly in marketing content
Help customers adopt and keep using digital banking services
Apply fair-marketing, data consent and online content rules to everyday marketing work

runningCase.name: Bank A's campus app campaign
runningCase.text: Meron Alemu is a digital marketing officer at Bank A, a fictional Ethiopian commercial bank. Her team must grow active use of the bank's mobile app among university students, starting with Entoto Hills University, a fictional campus of about 18,000 students in Addis Ababa. Through the course the team reads funnel numbers, picks channels, writes copy in Amharic, Afaan Oromo and English, explains fees honestly, runs an ambassador desk and handles a fake channel and a rumour. The capstone is a one-week content plan and three posts promoting the app to students, with a budget of Birr 36,000 and a target of 300 new active users.

modules.title: Digital marketing basics and the Ethiopian audience
modules.summary: Learn the digital marketing funnel from awareness to advocacy, the difference between owned, earned and paid media, and who the Ethiopian digital customer really is.
objectives: Explain the five stages of the digital marketing funnel and what a bank wants at each stage
Tell owned, earned and paid media apart and give a bank example of each
Describe the Ethiopian digital audience: mobile-first, data-cost conscious, multilingual and social-media led
Read simple funnel numbers and spot where customers drop out

lessons.title: Why banks market digitally
body: Digital marketing is the use of online and mobile channels, such as social media, SMS, websites and app stores, to make people aware of a product, persuade them to try it and keep them using it. For a bank, the product being marketed is often a digital one: the mobile app, mobile banking, a wallet or a digital loan. The marketing and the product live on the same phone.

This is good news and a responsibility at the same time. A customer can see a post on Telegram, tap a link and open an account in minutes, so the distance between a message and a decision is very short. That is why every post a bank publishes must be clear and honest: it is not just an advert, it is the first step of a financial decision.
points: Digital channels let a small team reach many people at a low cost per person
Results can be measured almost in real time: views, clicks, downloads, sign-ups
Messages can be tailored by language, region, age and interest
Mistakes also spread fast, so review before you publish

example.title: From flyer to Telegram
example.text: For years, Bank A's Hawassa branch promoted its savings account with printed flyers handed out on market days. When Meron Alemu, a digital marketing officer, moved the same offer to the branch's Telegram channel and a short video on TikTok, the branch could see for the first time how many people watched, how many tapped the link and how many opened an account. The flyers had no such data. The branch kept a few flyers for older customers and moved most of the budget to channels it could measure.

regulation.source: NBE financial consumer protection directive FCP/01/2020 (reported)
regulation.text: The NBE's financial consumer protection directive is reported to require fair, clear and non-misleading advertising of financial products. Because a digital post can lead straight to an account opening or a loan, treat every post as a customer disclosure, not only as an advert.

lessons.tip: Before you plan any post, write one sentence: who is it for, and what do you want them to do next?

lessons.title: The funnel: awareness to advocacy
body: The marketing funnel describes the path a person takes from first hearing about a product to recommending it to others. At each stage fewer people remain, which is why it is drawn as a funnel. A good plan has content for every stage, not only for the top.

In digital banking the funnel does not end at download. A customer who installs the app but never logs in is not a win. The stages that matter most for a bank are activation (the first real transaction) and retention (using the service month after month). Advocacy follows when satisfied customers tell friends, share posts and leave good reviews.

items.label: Awareness
items.text: The person sees the bank's message, for example a TikTok video about the app.

items.label: Consideration
items.text: They compare: is it safe, is it free, does it work on my phone?

items.label: Conversion
items.text: They download the app and register.

items.label: Activation and retention
items.text: They make a first transfer and keep using it each month.

items.label: Advocacy
items.text: They recommend it, share it or rate it in the app store.

worked.title: Reading a campus funnel

rows.label: People reached by posts in one month
Registered and verified identity (60% of downloads)
Made a first transaction within 30 days (50% of registered)

worked.note: The biggest loss is between download and active use. More reach would make the top of the funnel bigger, but fixing onboarding and first-use help would make every Birr work harder.

lessons.tip: Always report the cost per active user, not only the cost per click or per download.

lessons.title: Owned, earned and paid media
body: Owned media are the channels the bank controls: its website, mobile app, official Facebook page, Telegram channel, YouTube channel and SMS list of consenting customers. They cost little to use but take time to grow an audience.

Paid media are channels where the bank pays for reach: boosted posts, ads on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok or YouTube, paid influencers and sponsored content. Earned media are what others say for free: customers sharing a post, a news story, a positive review or a student who tells classmates. Earned media is the most trusted, and it is earned by being useful and honest on owned and paid channels first.

items.label: Owned
items.text: Website, app, official pages, Telegram channel, opted-in SMS list.

items.label: Paid
items.text: Boosted posts, social ads, paid influencers, sponsored videos.

items.label: Earned
items.text: Shares, reviews, word of mouth, news coverage.

scenario.title: Where to spend a small budget
scenario.situation: Bank A's Bahir Dar branch has Birr 20,000 for one month to promote mobile banking. Its official Facebook page has 3,000 followers and its Telegram channel has 900 members. There is no budget for a second month.
scenario.question: What is the most sensible plan?
options: Post regularly on the owned page and channel, and use the Birr 20,000 to boost the two best posts to local adults, with a link to a clear how-to guide
Spend all of it on one celebrity influencer post and stop posting on owned channels
Do nothing on paid media and wait for customers to share posts
Buy a list of phone numbers and send bulk SMS
scenario.explain: Owned channels give a steady base and paid boosts extend the best content to new people at a controlled cost. One celebrity post is a big bet with no follow-up, waiting for shares alone is slow, and a bought number list raises consent and data protection problems.

lessons.tip: Paid media rents attention; owned media builds it. Plan both.

lessons.title: The Ethiopian digital audience
body: Most Ethiopian customers meet the internet on a smartphone, not a computer. Many use prepaid data bundles and watch their data cost closely, so heavy videos, large apps and long web pages can lose them. A World Bank telecom market assessment (2025) reports 4G coverage above 40 percent of the population by early 2025 and an average mobile broadband speed of about 4.5 Mbit/s, so many users are still on slower connections.

Telegram is widely used for news, groups and channels; Facebook remains the broad reach platform; TikTok is growing fast with young people; YouTube carries longer how-to videos. Customers speak Amharic, Afaan Oromo, Tigrinya, Somali and many other languages, and many prefer to read finance in their own language. Feature phone users are reached by SMS and USSD, not by social media.
points: Design for small screens and low data first
Use the language your audience actually reads
Do not forget feature phone users: SMS and USSD still matter
Trust is fragile: scams on social media make people wary of links

left.title: Smartphone user
items: Reached on Telegram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube
Can download the app from an app store
Responds to short video and images

right.title: Feature phone user
items: Reached by SMS and USSD menus
Needs simple text in the local language
Often helped by branch or agent staff

example.title: A data-light app launch
example.text: When Bank A refreshed its mobile app, the team noticed that many students in Mekelle and Jimma abandoned the download halfway. The app was large and campus Wi-Fi was busy. Marketing changed the message to tell students the exact size of the app and where to download it on campus Wi-Fi, and the product team released a lighter version. Completed downloads rose in the following weeks.

lessons.tip: Ask a colleague with an older, cheaper phone to test every post and link before it goes live.

lessons.title: What to measure
body: Every digital channel produces numbers, and not all of them matter. Reach and impressions tell you how many people saw something. Engagement (likes, comments, shares) tells you whether it interested them. Click-through rate is clicks divided by people reached. Conversion rate is the share who did what you wanted, such as registering.

For digital banking the numbers that matter most are activations (first real transaction), active users (customers who transacted in the last 30 or 90 days) and cost per active user. Likes are pleasant but a post with fewer likes and more activations is the better post.

visual.caption: The single number that tells you whether digital marketing is paying for itself.

scenario.title: Which post worked better?
scenario.situation: Two posts promoted the same app. Post A, a funny video, reached 50,000 people, got 4,000 likes and led to 60 active users. Post B, a 30-second how-to video in Amharic, reached 20,000 people, got 600 likes and led to 150 active users. Each cost Birr 6,000 to boost.
scenario.question: Which post should the team repeat and learn from?
options: Post A, because it had far more likes
Post A, because it reached more people
Neither, because likes were low in both
Post B, because it cost Birr 40 per active user against Birr 100 for Post A
scenario.explain: Birr 6,000 divided by 150 is Birr 40 per active user; Birr 6,000 divided by 60 is Birr 100. Reach and likes are useful signals, but the bank's goal is active users.

lessons.tip: Set up a tracking link for each post so you know which one brought each registration.

takeaways: Digital marketing for banks is part of the customer's financial decision, so it must be clear and honest
The funnel runs from awareness to advocacy, and for digital banking activation and retention matter most
Owned media builds an audience, paid media extends reach, earned media is the most trusted
Ethiopian customers are mostly mobile-first, data-cost conscious and multilingual; feature phone users need SMS and USSD
Judge campaigns by cost per active user, not by likes

quiz.q: Which funnel stage comes right after a customer registers for mobile banking?
options: Awareness
Consideration
Activation: the first real transaction
Advocacy
quiz.explain: Registration is conversion; the next step is activation, the first real use.

quiz.q: A customer review praising the bank's app in the app store is an example of:
options: Earned media
Paid media
Owned media
A direct SMS
quiz.explain: The bank did not pay for or publish it; the customer did, so it is earned.

quiz.q: Bank A spent Birr 30,000 and gained 250 active users. What is the cost per active user?
options: Birr 250
Birr 83
Birr 1,200
Birr 120
quiz.explain: 30,000 divided by 250 is Birr 120.

quiz.q: Which channel best reaches a feature phone user?
options: TikTok
SMS or USSD
YouTube
An app store listing
quiz.explain: Feature phones do not run social apps; SMS and USSD reach them.

quiz.q: Why should a campus post state the size of the app?
options: It is required on every post
It makes the app look more advanced
Many users watch data costs and may stop a large download
It improves the bank's capital ratio
quiz.explain: Data cost is a real barrier in Ethiopia, so being open about size helps people finish the download.

quiz.q: Which number matters most when judging a digital banking campaign?
options: Number of likes
Active users and cost per active user
Number of impressions
Number of posts published
quiz.explain: The goal is customers who use the service, so active users and their cost come first.

modules.title: Digital channels in Ethiopia
modules.summary: Know what each channel does best, from Facebook, Telegram, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn to SMS and USSD push, websites, app stores and influencers, and how to combine them.
objectives: Describe the strengths and limits of Facebook, Telegram, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn for bank marketing
Use SMS and USSD push with consent and within the bank's rules
Explain the role of the bank's website and app store listing in conversion
Choose and brief an influencer or student ambassador responsibly
Match channels to an audience and a goal

lessons.title: Facebook, Telegram, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn
body: Each platform has its own audience and style. Facebook gives broad reach across ages and regions and has detailed ad targeting. Telegram is where many Ethiopians follow channels and join groups; a bank channel works well for announcements, how-to guides and service updates. TikTok rewards short, lively vertical videos and is strongest with people under 30.

YouTube suits longer explainers, such as a three-minute walk-through of the app, and these videos can be embedded on the website. LinkedIn reaches professionals, business owners and job seekers, and suits employer branding, SME banking and thought leadership more than consumer offers. Instagram is used mostly by younger urban audiences and shares the same ad system as Facebook.

items.label: Facebook
items.text: Broad reach, all ages, strong ad targeting.

items.label: Telegram
items.text: Channels and groups, announcements, how-to guides.

items.label: TikTok
items.text: Short vertical video, young audience, trends.

items.label: YouTube
items.text: Longer explainers and tutorials.

items.label: LinkedIn
items.text: Professionals, SMEs, careers, expertise.

example.title: One message, four formats
example.text: To announce that students can open an account through the app, Meron's team made one core message and adapted it: a 20-second TikTok of a student opening an account between classes, a Telegram post with five numbered steps and a link, a Facebook carousel with the same steps in Amharic and English, and a two-minute YouTube tutorial. Each piece linked to the same landing page with its own tracking code.

lessons.tip: Never copy the same post to every platform unchanged. Keep the message, change the format.

lessons.title: Running an official Telegram channel safely
body: Fake bank channels and groups are a common scam in Ethiopia: fraudsters copy a bank's logo, promise loans or prizes and ask for PINs, OTPs or fees. An official channel must therefore be easy to verify. Link to it from the bank's website and app, use the same name and logo everywhere, and pin a message that explains what the bank will never ask for.

Use the channel for useful content: how-to guides, service hours, branch news, fraud warnings and product updates. Turn off or moderate comments in a way the team can manage, answer questions with a link to official help, and never discuss a customer's account details in public.
points: Pin a message: "We will never ask for your PIN, password or OTP"
Link the channel from the official website and app so customers can confirm it is real
Report fake channels using the platform's reporting tools
Move account questions to private, verified channels

scenario.title: A fake channel appears
scenario.situation: A student messages Bank A's official page: a Telegram channel using the bank's logo is offering "instant student loans of Birr 10,000, pay Birr 300 registration fee first". It has 4,000 members and is growing.
scenario.question: What should the digital marketing officer do first?
options: Ignore it, because the bank did not create it
Message the fake channel's admin to ask them to stop
Delete the student's message so others do not see it
Report it to the platform and the bank's fraud team, and post a clear warning on official channels linking to the verified channel
scenario.explain: Customers are at risk now, so the bank should warn them on verified channels and report the fake one. Ignoring it or deleting the warning lets more people be cheated, and contacting the fraudster does not protect anyone.

lessons.tip: Search for your bank's name on Telegram every week to spot copycat channels early.

lessons.title: SMS and USSD push
body: SMS reaches almost every phone, including feature phones, and is read quickly. Banks use it for service alerts and, with consent, for marketing. USSD push sends a menu prompt to the customer's phone, for example to complete a registration or confirm a payment. Both are short and direct, so every character counts.

Marketing SMS needs the customer's consent and an easy way to opt out. Send at sensible hours, use the bank's registered sender name so customers can tell it apart from scams, and never include a link that asks for a PIN. Rules on bulk SMS and sender names are set by the telecom regulator; check the current rules with your compliance team before a campaign.

regulation.source: Ethiopian Communications Authority rules on bulk SMS (to be confirmed with compliance)
regulation.text: Bulk and promotional SMS are subject to telecom regulator rules, including registered sender identities. The exact current requirements were not confirmed for this course. Treat consent, a working opt-out and the registered sender name as the minimum, and confirm the rest with your compliance team.

worked.title: Comparing two channels for the same goal (illustrative figures)

rows.label: SMS to 10,000 opted-in customers at an assumed Birr 0.50 each
Customers who activated mobile banking after the SMS (1.2%)
New activations attributed to the video

worked.note: For existing customers who already trust the bank, an SMS can be cheaper per activation. For new customers, social media reaches people the SMS list cannot. The figures here are an example, not market prices.

lessons.tip: Write marketing SMS in the customer's language and keep it under one message length so it arrives in one piece.

lessons.title: Website, landing pages and app store listings
body: Social posts create interest, but conversion happens on a landing page or an app store page. A good landing page loads fast on a weak connection, says in one line what the product does, shows the fees and requirements, and has one clear button. A slow or confusing page wastes all the money spent bringing people to it.

The app store listing is often the last thing a customer reads before downloading. Use a clear name and description in Amharic and English, show real screenshots, state the app size and answer reviews politely. A warning about fake apps and a link from the official website help customers download the real app.

items.label: Post
items.text: A short video or image with one message.

items.label: Landing page
items.text: One line on benefits, fees, requirements, one button.

items.label: App store
items.text: Official listing, real screenshots, app size, reviews.

items.label: Onboarding
items.text: Register, verify identity, first transaction.

example.title: Answering a one-star review
example.text: A student, Liya Getachew, gave Bank A's app one star: "OTP never arrives". The team replied the same day in her language, apologised, explained how to check the registered phone number and gave the official help line. They also passed the issue to the product team. A week later Liya changed her rating to four stars and others read the reply too.

lessons.tip: Reply to every negative review within two working days. Other customers read the replies.

lessons.title: Influencers and student ambassadors
body: Influencers and ambassadors borrow trust from people the audience already follows. A respected campus vlogger or a well-known student leader can explain the app in a way that feels natural. That trust is exactly why the bank must brief them carefully: whatever they say is treated as the bank's message.

Give each influencer a written brief with the approved facts, fees and what they must not say, require them to show that the post is a paid partnership, and review the script or video before it goes out. Choose people whose values and past content fit a bank, and avoid anyone whose content includes hate speech, gambling or political campaigning.

left.title: Good influencer brief
items: Clear call to action and link

scenario.title: The influencer's script
scenario.situation: A popular TikTok creator with many followers at Addis Ababa campuses sends a draft script: "Download Bank A's app and get a loan instantly, no questions asked!" The bank's student loan product requires an assessment and has fees.
scenario.question: What should the marketing officer do?
options: Approve it, because energetic scripts perform better
Ask for a revised script that describes the product accurately, mentions that conditions and fees apply and links to the details
Approve it but add a small disclaimer at the end of the video
Cancel the partnership and never work with influencers
scenario.explain: "No questions asked" is misleading, and a small disclaimer does not fix a false main message. Influencers can still work well when the script is accurate.

lessons.tip: Keep a signed copy of each influencer brief and the approved final content.

lessons.title: Choosing the channel mix
body: Start from the audience and the goal, then pick channels. For university students, TikTok, Telegram and Instagram build awareness, a landing page and the app store convert, and in-app messages and Telegram support help them keep using the app. For small merchants, Telegram groups, SMS, agents and branch staff often matter more.

A simple channel plan lists each channel, its job in the funnel, the content type, how often you post, the budget and the measure of success. Review it weekly and move money towards the channels that bring active users.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. ONPS/09/2023 (Payment Instrument Issuer, Amendment)
regulation.text: The amendment raised the daily mobile money wallet balance limit from Birr 30,000 to Birr 75,000 and set a daily aggregate transaction limit of Birr 150,000, with exemptions such as utility, tax and bulk payments. Marketing for wallet features must not promise more than these limits allow; the directive was further amended by ONPS/10/2025, so check the current limits before quoting them.

lessons.tip: Give every channel one clear job in the funnel. A channel without a job becomes a cost without a result.

takeaways: Each platform has a different audience and format: adapt the message, do not paste it everywhere
Official channels must be easy to verify because fake bank channels are common
SMS and USSD reach every phone but need consent, an opt-out and a registered sender name
Conversion happens on the landing page and app store listing, so make them fast and clear
Influencers must be briefed, labelled as paid and reviewed before posting

quiz.q: Which platform is best suited to a three-minute walk-through of the mobile app?
options: SMS
YouTube
USSD push
A printed flyer
quiz.explain: Longer tutorials fit YouTube and can be embedded on the website.

quiz.q: What should a bank's official Telegram channel pin to protect customers?
options: The admin's personal phone number
A list of customers who won prizes with their account numbers
A notice that the bank never asks for PINs, passwords or OTPs
Nothing; pinning is not needed
quiz.explain: A clear warning helps customers recognise scams that copy the bank.

quiz.q: Which is a minimum condition for a marketing SMS campaign?
options: A link that asks for the customer's PIN
Sending after midnight when the network is free
A bought list of numbers
Customer consent with a working opt-out
quiz.explain: Consent and opt-out protect customers and keep the bank within data protection rules.

quiz.q: A campaign gets many clicks but few registrations. Where should the team look first?
options: The landing page and app store listing
The bank's capital plan
The number of likes
The font on the bank's letterhead
quiz.explain: Clicks that do not convert usually point to a slow or confusing landing page or listing.

quiz.q: Under ONPS/09/2023, the daily wallet balance limit was raised to:
options: Birr 30,000
Birr 75,000
Birr 10,000
quiz.explain: The directive raised it from Birr 30,000 to Birr 75,000; Birr 150,000 is the daily aggregate transaction limit.

quiz.q: An influencer post for the bank should:
options: Show that it is a paid partnership and use approved facts
Hide the sponsorship so it feels natural
Promise guaranteed loans
Be posted without review to save time
quiz.explain: Disclosure and approved content keep the message honest and protect the bank's reputation.

modules.title: Creating clear, compliant content
modules.summary: Write copy, design visuals and make short videos that explain bank products, rates and fees clearly in Amharic, English and other local languages.
objectives: Write short, plain copy for a financial product with one message and one call to action
Design visuals and short videos that work on small screens and low data
Adapt content into Amharic, Afaan Oromo and other languages without losing meaning
Explain interest, fees and the total cost of a product clearly and honestly
Check content against a simple compliance checklist before publishing

lessons.title: Copywriting for finance
body: Good financial copy is short, plain and specific. It says what the product does for the customer, what it costs and what to do next. Replace bank jargon with everyday words: "send money to any bank from your phone" is clearer than "interbank fund transfer functionality".

Every post should have one main message and one call to action. If a post tries to sell the app, a savings account and a loan at the same time, the reader remembers none of them. Honest specifics also build trust: "No fee for transfers within Bank A" is better than "Amazing low fees!".

items.label: Clear
items.text: Plain words, no jargon.

items.label: Local
items.text: In the reader's language and context.

items.label: Exact
items.text: Real fees, conditions and limits.

items.label: Action
items.text: One next step: download, register, call.

items.label: Reviewed
items.text: Checked by compliance before posting.

example.title: Rewriting a post
example.text: Meron's first draft read: "Experience next-generation seamless digital banking with Bank A's revolutionary super app!" Students in a test group could not say what it did. The rewrite read: "Pay your cafe bill, top up airtime and get money from home, all from your phone. Free to download. Open an account in 10 minutes with your student ID and Fayda number." Nine out of ten testers could explain it back.

lessons.tip: Read your copy aloud to someone outside the bank. If they cannot repeat the message, rewrite it.

lessons.title: Visuals and short video
body: On a phone, people decide in a second or two whether to stop scrolling. Use one strong image, large readable text, real Ethiopian faces and places, and the bank's brand colours. Show the product being used: a hand on a phone paying at a campus cafe tells the story faster than an abstract graphic.

Short vertical videos of 15 to 45 seconds work best on TikTok, Instagram and Facebook. Put the main point in the first three seconds, add on-screen captions because many people watch without sound, and keep files light for data-conscious viewers. Never show real customer account details, PINs or balances on screen, even as a joke.

items.label: 0 to 3 seconds
items.text: Hook: the problem or benefit, in words on screen.

items.label: 3 to 20 seconds
items.text: Show it: the steps in the app, with captions.

items.label: 20 to 30 seconds
items.text: Cost and conditions, stated clearly.

items.label: Last seconds
items.text: Call to action and the official link or channel.

scenario.title: A video showing a screen
scenario.situation: A student ambassador films a lively video of himself sending money to a friend through Bank A's app. In two frames, his full account number and balance of Birr 2,350 are clearly visible.
scenario.question: What should happen before the video is posted?
options: Post it, because it is his own account and he agreed
Post it, because the balance is small
Add a caption asking viewers not to copy the number
Blur or re-film the frames so no account details appear, then review the full video again
scenario.explain: Showing account details teaches bad security habits and can enable fraud, whoever owns the account. The safe fix is to remove them and review again.

lessons.tip: Use a demo account with dummy data when filming any app screen.

lessons.title: Writing in local languages
body: Many customers understand finance better in their first language. Content in Amharic reaches a wide audience, and Afaan Oromo, Tigrinya, Somali and other languages reach regions where Amharic or English posts are ignored. A simple Amharic line such as "ገንዘብዎን በስልክዎ ያስተዳድሩ" (manage your money on your phone) can be more powerful than a long English paragraph.

Do not rely on machine translation for financial terms. Have a fluent speaker who understands banking write or check each version, keep a glossary of approved terms (interest, fee, transfer, PIN, OTP) in each language, and make sure the fees and conditions say exactly the same thing in every version.
points: Keep an approved glossary of financial terms in each language
Check that numbers, fees and dates match in every language version
Use the script and style the audience reads; Afaan Oromo uses the Latin script (Qubee)
Test with real readers from the region

example.title: The fee that changed in translation
example.text: An English post said "Birr 5 fee for transfers to other banks". The Afaan Oromo version, translated in a hurry, left out the word for "other banks" and seemed to say every transfer cost Birr 5. Customers in Adama complained about a fee they were never charged. The team corrected the post, apologised, and added a second reviewer for every language version.

lessons.tip: Build the glossary once with compliance and product teams, then reuse it in every campaign.

lessons.title: Explaining rates and fees clearly
body: The most important part of financial content is the cost. Customers need to know the interest rate, every fee and the total amount they will pay or earn. Since NBE Directive NBE/INT/13/2026 (January 2026), banks set deposit and lending rates freely, which makes clear disclosure even more important: customers can only compare if banks state costs in a comparable way.

Avoid headline tricks. "Only 3%" for a 30-day digital loan sounds cheap, but as an annual rate it is far higher. Show the fee in Birr, the period and the total to repay, and where the rules require it, the annual percentage rate. If a savings rate is "up to" a figure, say what a typical customer will actually earn.

worked.title: Explaining a 30-day digital loan

rows.label: Clear copy
rows.value: "Borrow Birr 5,000 for 30 days, repay Birr 5,150. Fee Birr 150, equal to about 36.5% a year."

worked.note: "Only 3%" hides the time period. Showing the Birr amount, the period and the annual equivalent lets the customer compare fairly. The 3% fee is an example for this exercise, not a market rate.

regulation.source: NBE financial consumer protection directive FCP/01/2020 (reported)
regulation.text: The directive is reported to require that banks advertise in a fair, clear and non-misleading way, disclose the cost of credit including an annual percentage rate, and use customer data responsibly. Its exact wording was not confirmed for this course, so follow your bank's compliance guidance on the required format.

scenario.title: The "up to" savings rate
scenario.situation: Bank A's new student savings account pays 7% a year on balances above Birr 50,000 and 5% below that. A draft post says: "Earn up to 7% on your savings!" Most students keep less than Birr 5,000.
scenario.question: How should the post be changed?
options: State both rates and the Birr 50,000 threshold so students see they will most likely earn 5%
Keep it, because "up to" is technically true
Remove all rates and just say "great returns"
Change it to 7% for everyone without telling product
scenario.explain: "Up to 7%" creates the impression most students will get 7%, which is misleading for this audience. Vague claims are worse, and changing the product without approval is not marketing's decision.

lessons.title: The pre-publish checklist
body: Before any post goes live, run a short checklist. Is the main claim true and can we prove it? Are fees, rates and conditions stated or clearly linked? Is the language correct in every version? Does it show any customer data? Is there a link only to official pages? Has compliance approved it where the bank's policy requires?

A checklist is fastest when built into the workflow: a shared folder where drafts wait for a second reviewer, and a log of who approved what and when. This protects customers, protects the bank and protects the staff member who posted.

items.label: Truth
items.text: Every claim is accurate and can be proven.

items.label: Cost
items.text: Fees, rates and conditions are clear or linked.

items.label: Language
items.text: Each language version says the same thing.

items.label: Privacy
items.text: No customer data, real account numbers or PINs.

items.label: Links
items.text: Only official pages and app stores.

items.label: Approval
items.text: Second reviewer and compliance sign-off logged.

example.title: A checklist saves a launch
example.text: The night before a campus launch, the checklist caught that a Telegram post linked to a lookalike web address a staff member had typed by mistake. The link was fixed before posting. Without the check, the bank would have sent thousands of students to a page it did not control.

lessons.tip: Keep the checklist to one screen. A checklist nobody uses protects nobody.

takeaways: Good financial copy is clear, local, exact, action-focused and reviewed
Short vertical video should make its point in three seconds, use captions and stay light on data
Local language content needs fluent, banking-aware review and an approved glossary
Always state costs in Birr with the period, and annual rates where required; avoid "only" and "up to" tricks
Never show real customer data or PINs; use a pre-publish checklist and log approvals

quiz.q: Which line is the clearest copy for a mobile transfer feature?
options: "Leverage our interbank fund transfer functionality"
"Revolutionary seamless super app"
"Send money to any bank from your phone"
"Banking reimagined"
quiz.explain: Plain, specific words tell the customer exactly what they can do.

quiz.q: A 30-day loan has a 2% fee. What is its simple annual equivalent?
options: 2% a year
About 24% a year
About 12% a year
About 60% a year
quiz.explain: 2% x 365 / 30 is about 24.3% a year.

quiz.q: Why add captions to short videos?
options: Many people watch without sound
Captions make files larger
Platforms ban videos without captions
Captions replace the need for review
quiz.explain: Captions carry the message when the sound is off, which is common on phones.

quiz.q: What is the safest way to film an app demo?
options: Use a staff member's real account
Use a customer's account with permission
Blur nothing; viewers will not notice
Use a demo account with dummy data
quiz.explain: Dummy data removes any risk of exposing real account details.

quiz.q: An Afaan Oromo version of a post states a different fee from the English version. What went wrong?
options: Afaan Oromo cannot express fees
The translation was not checked against the approved facts
Fees should only be in English
Nothing; small differences are normal
quiz.explain: Every language version must carry the same facts, checked by a fluent reviewer.

quiz.q: Since NBE/INT/13/2026, banks set deposit and lending rates freely. What does this mean for marketing?
options: Banks no longer need to state rates
All banks must advertise the same rate
Clear, comparable disclosure of costs matters even more
A minimum deposit rate must be shown in every post
quiz.explain: With free rate setting, customers rely on clear disclosure to compare offers.

modules.title: Driving digital adoption and usage
modules.summary: Turn downloads into active customers through simple onboarding journeys, in-branch digital ambassadors, sensible incentives and education for first-time users.
objectives: Map an onboarding journey and find the steps where customers drop out
Run an in-branch digital ambassador programme
Design incentives that encourage real use without attracting abuse
Educate first-time users on safe digital banking
Measure activation and 30-day retention

lessons.title: Onboarding journeys
body: An onboarding journey is every step from download to first transaction: install, register, verify identity, set a PIN, link or open an account and make a first transfer or payment. Each extra screen or confusing word loses customers. Marketing and product teams should walk the journey together on a cheap phone and a slow connection.

Messages should follow the journey. A welcome SMS after registration, an in-app tip to make a first airtime top-up, and a reminder after three days if nothing has happened all help. Each message must be useful, short and sent only to customers who agreed to receive it.

items.label: Download
items.text: Official store, app size stated.

items.label: Register
items.text: Phone number and OTP.

items.label: Verify
items.text: ID or Fayda number, selfie if required.

items.label: Secure
items.text: Set a PIN, learn never to share it.

items.label: First use
items.text: Top up airtime or pay a small bill.

items.label: Habit
items.text: Regular payments, transfers and savings.

worked.title: Where students drop out

rows.label: Biggest drop
rows.value: Logged in but no first transaction: 460 students

worked.note: The weakest step is first use, not download. A clear first-use prompt, such as a small airtime top-up, and a how-to video will do more than extra reach.

lessons.tip: Test the full journey yourself every month. Apps and rules change, and so do the pain points.

lessons.title: In-branch digital ambassadors
body: A digital ambassador is a trained staff member, intern or student who helps customers install the app, register and make their first transaction, in the branch or at an event. Many Ethiopian customers, especially first-time users and older people, trust a person more than a video.

Ambassadors must follow strict rules: the customer holds the phone and types the PIN, the ambassador never asks for or writes down a PIN or OTP, and every customer leaves knowing how to get help. Track each ambassador's activations, not just registrations, and reward helpful service rather than pushing.
points: The customer types their own PIN and OTP, always
Use a quiet corner or desk, not a crowded queue
Finish with a real first transaction and a fraud warning
Record activations per ambassador and follow up after a week

example.title: The Saturday desk in Dessie
example.text: Bank A's Dessie branch set up a digital desk every Saturday morning staffed by Abebe Kassa and two student interns. Customers who came to withdraw cash were offered help to install the app. In two months, the desk registered 640 customers, and 410 of them were still transacting a month later, a better retention rate than the bank's online campaign because each customer left having made a real transfer.

scenario.title: The busy ambassador
scenario.situation: During a crowded campus event, an ambassador is helping a queue of students. To go faster, he offers to type in each student's OTP and set a default PIN of 1234 that they can change later.
scenario.question: What should the supervisor do?
options: Stop the practice at once: students must type their own OTP and choose their own PIN, and the team should slow down or add helpers
Allow it, because students can change the PIN later
Allow it only for students who agree
Ask him to write the PINs on paper so students do not forget
scenario.explain: Staff handling OTPs or setting PINs breaks basic security and exposes the bank and students to fraud. Speed is never a reason to bypass it.

lessons.tip: Give each ambassador a printed card listing what they must never ask for.

lessons.title: Incentives that build real use
body: Incentives such as airtime, cashback on a first payment or a small prize draw can move people from download to first use. They work best when tied to a real action, such as a first bill payment, rather than to registration alone, which can attract people who register and never return.

Watch for abuse: people registering several times with different numbers, or staff registering relatives just to earn a bonus. Set clear terms, one reward per verified customer, an end date and a cap on the total budget. Publish the terms where customers can read them, and pay rewards on time.

worked.title: Is the cashback worth it?

rows.label: First payments expected in the month
Assumed yearly fee and float income per active student

worked.note: If the assumptions hold, each retained student brings more than the reward cost within a year. The team should check the actual 90-day retention before extending the offer.

scenario.title: Paying for registrations
scenario.situation: A branch manager proposes paying Birr 30 airtime for every app registration, with no further condition, to hit a quarterly target of 5,000 registrations.
scenario.question: What is the main problem with this design?
options: Airtime is not allowed as a reward
Birr 30 is too generous for any customer
Registrations are not part of the funnel
It rewards sign-ups that may never be used and invites multiple fake registrations
scenario.explain: Tying the reward to a real first transaction, with one reward per verified customer, buys active users rather than empty accounts.

lessons.tip: Reward the behaviour you want to see in month three, not only on day one.

lessons.title: Educating first-time users
body: Many new digital customers have never used an app for money. They worry about pressing the wrong button, losing money or being cheated. Short, friendly education removes that fear: a 30-second video on how to check a balance, a Telegram post on what to do if a transfer fails, and a clear help line.

Fraud awareness belongs in every education message. Teach customers that the bank never asks for their PIN or OTP, that prize calls asking for a fee are scams, and that apps should be downloaded only from official stores. NBE Instruction FCPED/142/26 (April 2026) requires microfinance institutions to run customer fraud awareness campaigns, which shows the regulator's focus on this topic.

items.label: Protect your PIN
items.text: Never share it, not even with bank staff.

items.label: Spot scams
items.text: Prize calls asking for a fee are fraud.

items.label: Official app only
items.text: Download from the official store or website link.

items.label: Get help
items.text: Call the official number if a transfer fails.

regulation.text: The instruction requires microfinance institutions to run customer fraud awareness campaigns. It applies to MFIs, but bank marketing teams can follow the same good practice and build fraud awareness into every digital adoption campaign.

example.title: Grandmother's first transfer
example.text: Almaz Tadesse, a retired teacher in Gondar, received money from her son in Addis Ababa only by going to the branch. A digital ambassador showed her the app in Amharic, she typed her own PIN, and together they checked a test transfer of Birr 100. The ambassador gave her a printed card with the help line and the words "The bank will never ask for your PIN". She now checks her balance each week from home.

lessons.title: Using customer data for adoption campaigns
body: Adoption campaigns often use customer data: who has the app but has not used it, who withdraws cash every week, who receives remittances. Using this data to send a helpful nudge can be good service, but only within data protection rules and the bank's own policy.

Collect consent for marketing messages, use data only for the purpose the customer was told about, let customers opt out easily and keep lists secure. Never share customer lists with influencers, agencies or ambassadors unless the bank's legal team has approved a proper agreement.

regulation.source: Personal Data Protection Proclamation (2024), as reported
regulation.text: Ethiopia's personal data protection law governs the collection and processing of personal data. As reported for this course, it requires a lawful basis such as consent for processing, including for direct marketing and profiling, and gives individuals rights over their data. Confirm the bank's consent wording and opt-out process with the legal team.

lessons.tip: If you would be uncomfortable explaining to the customer how you picked them for a message, do not send it.

takeaways: Walk the onboarding journey on a cheap phone and find the step where customers drop out
Digital ambassadors build trust, but the customer always types their own PIN and OTP
Tie incentives to real first use, one per verified customer, with a cap and clear terms
Every education message should include fraud awareness
Use customer data for nudges only with consent and within data protection rules

quiz.q: Out of 1,000 students who logged in, 540 made a first transaction. What is the activation rate?
quiz.explain: 540 divided by 1,000 is 54%.

quiz.q: During assisted onboarding, who types the customer's PIN?
options: The customer, always
The ambassador, to save time
The branch manager
Anyone the customer trusts
quiz.explain: A PIN must be known only to the customer.

quiz.q: Which incentive design builds real use?
options: Airtime for every registration with no condition
Unlimited rewards for staff who register relatives
A prize for downloading the app twice
Birr 25 cashback on the first bill payment, one per verified customer
quiz.explain: Rewarding a real first transaction with limits attracts genuine users.

quiz.q: Which message should be in every first-time user education piece?
options: Share your PIN with the ambassador
The bank will never ask for your PIN or OTP
Download the app from any website
Pay a fee to receive prizes
quiz.explain: Fraud awareness protects new users who are the most frequent scam targets.

quiz.q: NBE Instruction FCPED/142/26 requires fraud awareness campaigns from:
options: Telecom operators
Universities
Microfinance institutions
Social media platforms
quiz.explain: The instruction is addressed to microfinance institutions.

quiz.q: Before sending app-reminder messages to customers who withdraw cash weekly, the team must check:
options: That the list has been shared with the influencer
That customers consented to marketing messages and can opt out
That the message is sent at night
Nothing; the bank owns the data
quiz.explain: Data protection rules require a lawful basis such as consent and an easy opt-out.

modules.title: The rules and the campus capstone
modules.summary: Apply fair-marketing, data consent and disinformation rules, then build a one-week content plan and three compliant posts promoting the bank's mobile app to university students.
objectives: Apply the main Ethiopian rules on fair advertising, data consent and online content to bank marketing
Recognise misleading claims and fix them
Handle comments, rumours and disinformation about the bank calmly and lawfully
Produce a one-week content plan and three compliant posts for university students
Assemble a content portfolio for assessment

lessons.title: Fair marketing rules
body: Bank marketing in Ethiopia sits under several layers of rules. The National Bank of Ethiopia Proclamation No. 1359/2025 gives the NBE a consumer protection role. The NBE's financial consumer protection directive (FCP/01/2020, reported) sets expectations for fair, clear and non-misleading advertising, cost disclosure and data use. Ethiopia's advertisement law sets general standards for all adverts, such as truthfulness and respect for the public.

Other laws touch digital marketing directly: the electronic transaction law gives legal validity to electronic records and signatures used in digital onboarding, the computer crime law covers misuse of systems and data, and the hate speech and disinformation law covers false or harmful content online. If the bank promotes shares or other securities, the Capital Market Proclamation No. 1248/2021 and ECMA rules on public offers apply as well.

regulation.source: National Bank of Ethiopia Proclamation No. 1359/2025, Art. 41 (consumer protection)
regulation.text: The proclamation gives the NBE a mandate for financial consumer protection. It is the legal basis for the NBE's consumer protection directives, which require banks to treat customers fairly, disclose costs clearly and advertise honestly.

items.label: NBE consumer protection
items.text: Fair, clear, non-misleading adverts and cost disclosure.

items.label: Advertisement law
items.text: Truthful adverts that respect the public.

items.label: Data protection
items.text: Consent for marketing and profiling.

items.label: Disinformation and computer crime
items.text: No false or harmful content, no misuse of systems.

items.label: Capital market rules
items.text: Apply when promoting shares or securities.

lessons.tip: When unsure whether a rule applies, ask compliance before posting, not after.

lessons.title: Avoiding misleading claims
body: A claim is misleading if it gives a false impression, even when each word is technically true. Common traps are "free" when fees apply later, "guaranteed" or "instant" loans that still need an assessment, "up to" rates most customers will never get, comparisons with other providers that cannot be proven, and fine print that contradicts the headline.

The fix is simple: state the main condition next to the claim, use real figures, and keep proof on file. Comparisons with telebirr, M-PESA or other banks are risky unless the facts are current, verified and fair; at Foundational level, focus on your own product's benefits instead.

right.title: Clear and fair
items: "Free to download. Transfers within Bank A cost nothing."
"Apply in the app. Decision usually within a day. Fees apply."
"5% a year, 7% on balances over Birr 50,000"
"No fee for transfers within Bank A"

scenario.title: The competitor comparison
scenario.situation: A colleague wants a TikTok video saying "Bank A is faster and cheaper than every mobile wallet in Ethiopia". There is no recent, verified comparison of speed or fees.
scenario.question: What is the best response?
options: Post it, because everyone exaggerates
Post it with "we think" at the start
Post it but delete it if a competitor complains
Drop the comparison and highlight Bank A's own verified benefits, such as its actual transfer fee
scenario.explain: Unproven comparisons are misleading and can harm trust and invite complaints. Hedging words or deleting later do not fix a claim the bank cannot support.

lessons.tip: For every claim, ask: can I show the proof today?

lessons.title: Comments, rumours and disinformation
body: Social media brings comments, complaints and sometimes false rumours, such as a claim that the bank is closing or that the app steals data. Respond quickly, calmly and with facts from official sources. Do not argue, insult or reveal any customer information in public replies. Move individual complaints to private, verified channels.

The bank's own content must never spread false information or content that targets people by ethnicity, religion or politics. Keep marketing neutral: no political messages, no jokes about groups, no unverified news. Ethiopia's hate speech and disinformation law makes this a legal matter as well as a reputational one.

regulation.source: Hate Speech and Disinformation Prevention Proclamation (2020); Advertisement Proclamation; Computer Crime Proclamation, as cited in the course specification
regulation.text: These laws set limits on harmful and false content, on advertising standards and on the misuse of computer systems and data. Their article numbers were not confirmed for this course. In practice, bank content must be truthful, respectful of all groups and politically neutral, and staff must not access or use systems or data beyond their authority.

scenario.title: A rumour in the comments
scenario.situation: A comment on Bank A's Facebook post claims, "This bank's app is stealing money from students, my friend lost Birr 3,000!" It has 200 likes. You do not know the facts of the friend's case.
scenario.question: What is the best first reply?
options: Delete the comment and block the user
A calm public reply that the bank takes this seriously, an invitation to contact the official help line or message the page privately, and a reminder never to share a PIN or OTP
Reply that the friend must have shared his PIN, so it is his fault
Post the friend's account history to prove him wrong
scenario.explain: A calm, factual reply shows other readers the bank cares and moves the case to a private channel. Deleting looks like hiding, blaming is unfair without facts, and posting account data breaches privacy.

example.title: A closure rumour
example.text: A false message spread on Telegram that Bank A's Dire Dawa branch would close and freeze accounts. Within an hour the bank posted an official notice in Amharic, Afaan Oromo, Somali and English on its verified channels, branch staff answered calls with the same words, and the manager recorded a short video at the open branch. The rumour faded within a day.

lessons.title: Capstone: the one-week campus content plan
body: The capstone brings the course together. Working as Meron's team at Bank A, you prepare a one-week content plan to promote the mobile app to students at Entoto Hills University, a fictional campus of about 18,000 students. The goal for the week is 300 new active student users, with a budget of Birr 30,000 for boosted posts and Birr 6,000 for first-payment cashback.

Your plan lists, for each day, the channel, the funnel stage, the content idea, the language, the call to action, the spend and the measure. It must use owned and paid media, at least two languages, a student ambassador event and a fraud awareness message, and every item must pass the pre-publish checklist.

items.label: Monday
items.text: Awareness: TikTok video "Pay at the campus cafe from your phone" (Amharic captions).

items.label: Tuesday
items.text: Consideration: Telegram post, five steps to open an account, fees stated.

items.label: Wednesday
items.text: Conversion: ambassador desk at the student centre, Facebook live reminder.

items.label: Thursday
items.text: Education: fraud awareness carousel in Amharic and Afaan Oromo.

items.label: Friday
items.text: Activation: in-app and SMS nudge to opted-in sign-ups, Birr 20 cashback on first payment.

items.label: Weekend
items.text: Advocacy: share-your-first-payment story with consent; review results.

worked.title: Capstone budget and targets

rows.label: Share of the campus reached as active users (300 / 18,000)

worked.note: The target is realistic for one week and gives a clear benchmark. If Wednesday's ambassador desk brings more activations per Birr than boosted posts, move Thursday's spend to a second desk.

example.title: How Meron's team chose the mix
example.text: In a test week on another campus, the team found that the ambassador desk produced active users at about Birr 70 each, against about Birr 150 for boosted TikTok posts. They kept TikTok for awareness, because the desk alone could not reach enough students, but planned two desk days for the Entoto Hills week and used Telegram to tell students where to find the desk.

lessons.title: Capstone: three posts and the portfolio
body: Write three posts for the week: a short video script for TikTok, a Telegram how-to post and a fraud awareness post. Each needs one message, one call to action, accurate costs, the right language and an official link. Run each through the checklist and record who reviewed it.

Your content portfolio for assessment includes the one-week plan, the three posts in final form, the completed checklist for each, and a half-page note on how you will measure results. The course ends with a quiz on the whole course. The suggested pass mark for the programme is 70%.
points: Post 1, TikTok script: hook in 3 seconds, steps on screen, cost line, call to action
Post 2, Telegram how-to: five numbered steps, fees, help line, official link
Post 3, fraud awareness: "We will never ask for your PIN or OTP" in two languages
Portfolio: plan, posts, checklists, measurement note

example.title: A model Telegram post
example.text: "Open your Bank A account from your phone in 10 minutes. 1. Download the app from the official store (link below, about 40 MB). 2. Register with your phone number. 3. Verify with your student ID and Fayda number. 4. Set your own PIN; never share it. 5. Top up airtime to try it. Transfers within Bank A: no fee. Help: our official line. We will never ask for your PIN or OTP." The same post in Amharic followed underneath, checked by a second reviewer.

scenario.title: Grading the posts
scenario.situation: A learner submits three posts. The TikTok script is lively and accurate, the Telegram post lists steps but omits fees, and the fraud post is in English only although the plan says two languages.
scenario.question: What feedback is most useful?
options: All three are fine because the TikTok script is good
Rewrite everything from the beginning
Strong TikTok script; add the transfer fee to the Telegram post and an Amharic version of the fraud post to meet the plan
Remove the fraud post because it does not sell the app
scenario.explain: Specific feedback tied to the checklist and the plan helps the learner fix the gaps. Fraud awareness is a required part of responsible adoption, not optional.

takeaways: Bank marketing must follow NBE consumer protection rules, the advertisement law, data protection and online content laws
A claim is misleading if it gives a false impression, so put the main condition next to every claim
Answer rumours and complaints calmly with facts and move individual cases to private channels
Keep all content truthful, respectful of every group and politically neutral
The capstone portfolio is a one-week plan, three checked posts and a measurement note

quiz.q: Which proclamation gives the NBE its consumer protection mandate (Art. 41)?
options: Capital Market Proclamation No. 1248/2021
National Bank of Ethiopia Proclamation No. 1359/2025
The advertisement law
The computer crime law
quiz.explain: Art. 41 of Proclamation No. 1359/2025 covers consumer protection.

quiz.q: "Free banking forever!" is a problem when:
options: The post is in Amharic
It is posted on Telegram
Some services carry fees
It has a call to action
quiz.explain: Saying "free" when fees apply gives a false impression.

quiz.q: When do the Capital Market Proclamation and ECMA rules apply to bank marketing?
options: For every savings account post
Only for SMS
Never
When the bank promotes shares or other securities
quiz.explain: Promotion of securities falls under capital market rules.

quiz.q: What is the best way to handle an individual complaint posted publicly?
options: Reply calmly in public and move the case to a private, verified channel
Post the customer's account details to explain
Delete it immediately
Argue until the customer withdraws it
quiz.explain: A calm public reply plus private follow-up protects both the customer and the bank's reputation.

quiz.q: In the capstone, Birr 36,000 is spent for 300 active users. What is the cost per active user?
options: Birr 100
Birr 300
Birr 120
Birr 36
quiz.explain: 36,000 divided by 300 is Birr 120.

quiz.q: Which item is NOT part of the capstone content portfolio?
options: A competitor price comparison
The one-week content plan
Three posts with completed checklists
A measurement note
quiz.explain: The portfolio is the plan, three checked posts and a measurement note.

exam.q: Bank A reached 80,000 students, 4,000 clicked, 1,200 downloaded, 900 registered and 450 made a first transaction. Which step lost the most people?
options: Download to registration
Reach to click
Registration to first transaction
Click to download
exam.explain: 76,000 people did not click, far more than any later step; the top of the funnel always loses the most, so the team also compares rates at each step.

exam.q: Using the same figures and a spend of Birr 36,000, what is the cost per active user?
options: Birr 80
Birr 40
Birr 30
Birr 120
exam.explain: 36,000 divided by 450 active users is Birr 80.

exam.q: A student shares Bank A's how-to video in her class Telegram group without being paid. This is:
options: Paid media
Owned media
A USSD push
Earned media
exam.explain: Unpaid sharing by customers is earned media.

exam.q: Two posts cost Birr 8,000 each. Post A brought 100 active users and Post B brought 160. How much cheaper per active user was Post B?
options: Birr 60
Birr 30
Birr 50
Birr 20
exam.explain: Post A: Birr 80; Post B: Birr 50; the difference is Birr 30.

exam.q: Bank A wants to reach older feature phone users in rural Amhara with a mobile banking reminder. Which channel fits best?
options: A TikTok trend
A LinkedIn article
SMS in Amharic to customers who opted in
A YouTube tutorial
exam.explain: Feature phone users are reached by SMS and USSD, in their language, with consent.

exam.q: A fake Telegram channel copies the bank's logo and asks for loan fees. Which action protects customers best?
options: Ignore it until it disappears
Pay the fake channel to stop
Ask staff to join it and argue with members
Warn customers on verified channels and report the fake channel
exam.explain: Prompt official warnings plus reporting limit the harm.

exam.q: A wallet promotion says "Keep up to Birr 100,000 in your wallet every day". Under ONPS/09/2023 as summarised in this course, what is wrong?
options: The daily wallet balance limit is Birr 75,000
There is no limit on wallets
The limit is Birr 30,000 for all customers
Wallets cannot hold Birr
exam.explain: ONPS/09/2023 raised the daily balance limit to Birr 75,000; promotions must not promise more, and current limits should be checked.

exam.q: An influencer's video says "Guaranteed loan, no questions asked" for a product that needs an assessment. What should the bank do?
options: Add a small disclaimer and approve
Approve because reach matters most
Require an accurate script before the post goes live
Let the influencer decide
exam.explain: A disclaimer cannot fix a misleading main claim.

exam.q: A digital loan of Birr 8,000 carries a 4% fee for 30 days. What should the post state as the total to repay?
options: Birr 8,320
Birr 8,040
Birr 8,400
Birr 8,032
exam.explain: 4% of 8,000 is Birr 320, so the total is Birr 8,320.

exam.q: What is the simple annual equivalent of that 4% fee for 30 days?
options: 4% a year
About 12% a year
About 33% a year
About 48.7% a year

exam.q: A savings account pays 4% below Birr 20,000 and 6% above it. Most target customers hold Birr 3,000. Which headline is fair?
options: "Earn up to 6%!"
"4% a year, 6% on balances over Birr 20,000"
"The best rate in Ethiopia"
"6% guaranteed"
exam.explain: Stating both tiers and the threshold avoids a false impression for this audience.

exam.q: The English and Tigrinya versions of a post give different transfer fees. What control was missing?
options: A bigger boost budget
A longer video
A fluent, banking-aware review against approved facts and a glossary
More hashtags
exam.explain: Every language version must be checked against the same approved facts.

exam.q: In a video, which practice is acceptable?
options: Showing a real account number briefly
Showing a demo account with dummy data
Showing a PIN being typed clearly
Showing a customer's balance with a smile emoji
exam.explain: Dummy data avoids exposing real customer or staff information.

exam.q: A branch sees 1,500 registrations but only 450 first transactions. What is the most effective next step?
options: Add a first-use prompt, a how-to video and ambassador follow-up
Double the reach budget
Stop the campaign
Pay for more registrations
exam.explain: The drop is after registration, so fixing first use gives the best return.

exam.q: An incentive pays Birr 20 per first bill payment for 1,000 customers. If 400 are still active after 90 days, what is the incentive cost per retained user?
options: Birr 20
Birr 40
Birr 25
Birr 50
exam.explain: Birr 20,000 divided by 400 is Birr 50.

exam.q: Which onboarding practice by a digital ambassador is acceptable?
options: Typing the OTP to save time
Guiding the customer while the customer types their own PIN and OTP
Setting the same default PIN for all students
Writing PINs on a list for safekeeping
exam.explain: Only the customer may know or enter their PIN and OTP.

exam.q: Before sending app reminders to customers chosen from transaction data, which check comes first?
options: Whether the influencer has the list
Whether the message can be sent at night
Marketing consent and a working opt-out
Whether the customers follow the bank on TikTok
exam.explain: Data protection rules require a lawful basis such as consent for marketing and profiling.

exam.q: A colleague wants to post "Cheaper than telebirr and every bank" with no verified data. What is the right decision?
options: Post it with "we think"
Post it and delete if challenged
Post it only on Telegram
Drop the comparison and promote Bank A's own verified fees
exam.explain: Unproven comparisons are misleading; hedging does not fix them.

exam.q: A false rumour says a branch is closing. Which response follows good practice?
options: Fast official notices on verified channels in local languages, with consistent answers from branch staff
Silence until the rumour stops
Reply to the rumour with jokes about the people spreading it
Ask customers to forward the bank's PIN warning to everyone
exam.explain: Quick, factual, consistent messages in the audience's languages stop rumours spreading.

exam.q: In the capstone, the ambassador desk produces active users at Birr 70 and TikTok boosts at Birr 150. What is the best adjustment?
options: Cancel the desk and spend everything on TikTok
Stop all paid posts and do nothing else
Add a second desk day and keep some TikTok for awareness
Move all money to SMS to non-customers
exam.explain: Shift budget towards the cheaper channel while keeping enough awareness to bring students to the desk.
